theory.title: Organizar planes y hablar del futuro
theory.explanation: En inglés hay varias formas de hablar del futuro y no son intercambiables en todos los casos. Utiliza be going to para intenciones ya decididas y predicciones basadas en evidencias; el present continuous para planes organizados con detalles concretos; will para decisiones espontáneas, promesas, ofrecimientos y predicciones generales; y may/might para posibilidades. En las frases temporales con when, as soon as, before y until, utiliza presente simple aunque hables del futuro: I'll call when I arrive (no when I will arrive). En el first conditional, if + presente simple va seguido de will + verbo base.
theory.tip: Piensa en cómo se tomó el plan: decisión ahora = I'll…; intención previa = I'm going to…; cita organizada = I'm meeting…; posibilidad = I might…; después de when/as soon as = presente simple.

patterns.label: Will: decisiones espontáneas
patterns.pattern: Will + verbo base para decisiones tomadas en el momento de hablar.
examples: The phone is ringing. I'll answer it.
It's cold. I'll close the window.

patterns.label: Going to: intenciones
patterns.pattern: Am/is/are going to + verbo base para planes o intenciones ya decididos.
examples: We're going to visit my aunt.
I'm going to book the tickets tonight.

patterns.label: Going to: predicciones con indicios
patterns.pattern: Be going to también expresa predicciones basadas en señales presentes.
examples: Look at those clouds. It's going to rain.
They're driving too fast. They're going to miss the turning.

patterns.label: Presente continuo: acuerdos fijados
patterns.pattern: Present continuous puede expresar planes futuros ya organizados, a menudo con hora o lugar.
examples: I'm meeting Sam at six.
We're having dinner at Nina's tonight.

patterns.label: Will: predicciones y ofrecimientos
patterns.pattern: Will expresa predicciones, promesas y ofrecimientos.
examples: I think you'll enjoy the show.
I'll carry that bag for you.

patterns.label: May/might: posibilidad
patterns.pattern: May/might + verbo base expresan posibilidad, sin certeza.
examples: We might take the earlier train.
It may be busy at the venue.

patterns.label: When/as soon as: conectores temporales
patterns.pattern: Para hablar del futuro después de when/as soon as/until, utiliza presente simple, no will.
examples: I'll call you when I arrive.
We'll leave as soon as the rain stops.

patterns.label: Primer condicional: posibilidades reales
patterns.pattern: If + presente simple, will + verbo base para una condición futura posible.
examples: If we book now, we'll get cheaper seats.
If she's free, she'll come with us.

patterns.label: Until/before: hasta y antes de
patterns.pattern: Until indica hasta que ocurra algo; before introduce una acción anterior.
examples: Wait here until I get back.
Check the time before you leave.

patterns.label: Organizar y cambiar planes
patterns.pattern: Utiliza present continuous para planes confirmados y expresiones como have to / might para cambios.
examples: I'm seeing the dentist on Friday.
We might have to postpone the trip.

content.passage: On Friday afternoon, Nina received a message from her cousin Tom. He was visiting the city for one night and wanted to meet. Nina was already having dinner with a colleague, so she wasn't sure what to do. She replied that she was meeting her colleague at seven and might be free later. Tom suggested going to an outdoor film screening, but the weather forecast showed heavy rain. Nina said they were going to check the programme and find an indoor event instead. While she was looking online, she found a small music festival at a local venue. She called Tom and said, 'I'll book two tickets now.' They agreed to meet outside the station at half past eight. Nina also made a backup plan: if the festival was full, they would go to a café nearby. When Tom arrived, his train was twenty minutes late, so Nina sent him the address and waited inside the station. They reached the venue just before the music started. The evening was different from what they had first planned, but both of them enjoyed it. Nina said she would remember to keep plans flexible next time.

items.prompt: Describe a plan you have already arranged for the near future.
items.modelAnswer: I'm meeting a friend from university next Saturday. We're having lunch at a restaurant near the station. After that, we're going to visit an exhibition. I've booked a table, but we haven't bought the tickets yet.

items.prompt: What do you do when a plan changes unexpectedly?
items.modelAnswer: First, I try to stay calm and find out what has changed. Then I contact the other people and suggest another option. If the weather is bad, for example, we might choose an indoor activity.

items.prompt: Invite a friend to do something this weekend.
items.modelAnswer: Are you free this weekend? I'm going to visit a new market on Saturday morning. Would you like to come along? We could have lunch nearby afterwards. Let me know when you can.

items.prompt: Explain the difference between a plan and a possibility using examples.
items.modelAnswer: A plan is something I've decided or arranged. For example, I'm meeting my sister on Friday. A possibility is less certain, so I might go to the cinema on Sunday, but I haven't decided yet.

items.prompt: Talk about a time you arrived late and what happened.
items.modelAnswer: Last month, I was going to meet a friend after work, but the bus ran late. I sent a message as soon as I realised. My friend waited in a café, and I arrived twenty minutes later.

items.prompt: How would you organise a visit from a friend who has only one day in your town?
items.modelAnswer: I'd ask what they enjoy doing and check the opening times in advance. We're going to visit the old town in the morning. We might go to a museum in the afternoon if we have enough time.

items.prompt: Make a plan for an outdoor activity and include a backup plan.
items.modelAnswer: I'm organising a walk by the coast for Sunday. We'll meet at the station at nine. If it rains, we'll postpone the walk and meet at a café instead. I'll check the forecast on Saturday.

items.prompt: Describe something you are looking forward to.
items.modelAnswer: I'm really looking forward to a family celebration next month. We're meeting at my grandparents' house, and everyone is bringing some food. I think it will be a lovely day.

items.prompt: Explain how you decide whether to accept a last-minute invitation.
items.modelAnswer: I check whether I'm available and whether I have enough time to get there. If I don't have other arrangements, I might accept. If I can't go, I reply quickly so the person can make another plan.

items.prompt: Speak about how to make plans successfully with a group of friends.
items.modelAnswer: I think clear communication is important. We should agree on a time and place and share the details in a group message. It's also useful to have a backup plan. If someone is delayed, they can let everyone know. That way, a small change won't spoil the day.

content.audioTranscript: Ella: Are we still going to the food festival on Saturday? Mark: I hope so, but the organisers have changed the schedule. The gates are opening later than we expected. Ella: Oh, I didn't know that. What time are you arriving? Mark: I'm taking the ten fifteen train, so I'll get there around eleven. Ella: I might come on the same train. I'll check the timetable tonight. Mark: Great. We should book our tickets in advance because it could get busy. Ella: Good idea. I'll buy mine now. Mark: If the weather gets worse, we might have to change our plans. Ella: That's fine. There's an indoor exhibition near the station. Mark: Perfect. I'll message you as soon as I know whether my friend is coming too.
